key_insight: PI-RADS-compliant prostate MRI can be performed at 0.55T with acceptable image quality and lesion detection, especially when deep learning reconstruction is used.
clinical_relevance: Low-field MRI could expand access to prostate imaging where 3T scanners are limited, while still supporting clinically usable diagnostic evaluation.
method: 15 healthy volunteers and 22 patients with suspected prostate cancer underwent bi-parametric 0.55T prostate MRI.
Protocol included tri-planar T2-weighted imaging and axial DWI aligned with PI-RADS guidance.
Deep learning reconstruction was applied and the low-field protocol was compared against 3T in patients.
evidence_signal: At 0.55T, 21/22 patients and all volunteers achieved acceptable diagnostic quality, and patient-level lesion detection was not significantly different from 3T.
watch_item: Results are from a small single-study cohort, so broader validation is needed before routine implementation across scanners and sites.
paper_title: Feasibility of PI-RADS Compliant Prostate MRI at 0.55T
